transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

My doctors keep telling me I’m too thin and need to eat more, but I honestly don’t see what all the fuss is about. I feel like I’m just being careful with my health and doing what's best for my heart.
Do you strongly fear gaining weight or feel very upset about the idea of being overweight, even if other people say you are too thin?

Yes, if I even think about eating rich foods like butter, I get a tight feeling in my chest and picture my arteries clogging up right away. When I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as "too thin" at all—I just see soft spots on my belly that I still need to trim down. To me, staying lean is just a matter of health and self-discipline, not something to worry about.
Do you avoid eating mainly because you are afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat, or is it more because you worry that certain foods will harm your health or heart?

Honestly, it’s really a mix of both. I do worry about my belly looking soft or popping out if I let myself go, but my main goal is protecting my heart and keeping my arteries clear so I don't end up like my friends. To me, keeping a strict limit on these foods is just the only disciplined way to stay healthy.
When you restrict food, is your main concern becoming fat or gaining weight, or is it mostly about avoiding specific foods because you believe they will damage your health or heart?

It is really a mix of both for me. I worry that "unsafe" foods like butter or ice cream will clog my arteries and damage my heart, but I also have a real fear of gaining weight and seeing my belly look soft or pop out. Keeping that weight off and maintaining this discipline is the only way I feel I can stay healthy and avoid heart disease.
When you think about eating less, which feels stronger: fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, or fear that certain foods will harm your health or heart?

For me, those two fears are completely tied together. Gaining weight and seeing my belly pop out feels like a direct threat to my heart, making me picture my arteries clogging up. When I think about foods like butter or ice cream, I get a tight feeling in my chest because I associate them with both weight gain and heart trouble, so staying lean feels like the only sensible way to protect my heart.
When you look in the mirror, do you feel you are actually too thin or underweight, or do you still feel you need to lose more weight even when others say you are very thin?

When I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as "too thin" at all, despite what the doctors say. I mostly just notice spots where my belly still looks soft and think I could stand to trim that down a bit more to keep my heart in good shape. To me, my weight isn't a danger—it's just a sign of good discipline and staying healthy.
Do you ever think you are too thin or underweight, or do you feel you still need to lose weight even when other people say you are already very thin?

When I look in the mirror, I really don't see "too thin"—I just see areas like my belly that still look soft and could stand to be trimmed down a bit more to protect my heart. While others worry, staying lean just feels like sensible discipline at my age, and I'm actually quietly pleased when I see the number on the scale go down.
Have you been intentionally restricting how much you eat, fasting, or exercising a lot to lose weight or prevent weight gain?

Yes, I do strictly limit what I eat. Most days I just make a small bowl of oatmeal for my wife and me to share in the morning, and then I'll just pick at some vegetables or half an apple later. I avoid rich foods like butter or ice cream to prevent weight gain and protect my heart, which just feels like sensible discipline for an older man who isn't very active anymore.
Do you ever feel that your body weight or shape is too low or that you need to gain weight, or do you mainly feel you should keep losing or maintaining weight to stay healthy?

I don't feel my weight is too low at all, and I certainly don't think I need to gain weight. When I look in the mirror, I just see soft areas on my belly that I could still trim down to protect my heart. Staying lean and keeping the scale down feels like healthy discipline, especially compared to the heart issues my buddies are facing.

When you think about your eating and weight, is your main concern becoming fat or gaining weight, or is it mainly about avoiding specific foods because you believe they will harm your health or heart?

It is really a combination of both, as I am deeply concerned about protecting my heart and keeping my arteries clear, especially after seeing my friends struggle with heart disease. However, I also get very anxious about gaining weight or seeing my belly look soft, and imagining eating "unsafe" foods like butter or ice cream makes me picture both clogged arteries and my belly popping out.
When you think about your eating, is your main fear gaining weight or becoming fat, or is it mostly that certain foods will harm your health or heart?

It’s really a mix of both fears for me. When I think about eating foods like butter or ice cream, I get a tight feeling in my chest because I picture my arteries clogging up and harming my heart. At the same time, I worry about my belly popping out or looking soft, which makes me feel like I need to keep trimming down.
If you had to choose, which is stronger for you: fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, or fear that eating certain foods will damage your health or heart?

I really can't separate the two because they are completely intertwined in my mind. Gaining weight or seeing my belly look soft is directly connected to my arteries clogging up and damaging my heart. If I even imagine eating butter or ice cream, I picture my belly popping out and my heart health failing all at once, because staying lean is how I keep my heart safe.
Do you believe you are already underweight or too thin, or do you still feel you need to lose more weight even when other people tell you you are very thin?

I don't see myself as underweight or too thin at all; when I look in the mirror, I just notice areas on my belly that still look soft and could be trimmed down to protect my heart. Staying lean feels like the safest, most sensible path for me at my age, so I'm actually quietly pleased when the number on the scale goes down. To me, it's just a sign of healthy discipline, not a medical problem.
If your doctor told you that your heart was completely healthy and the foods you avoid would not harm it, would you still strongly restrict food because of fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?

Even if my heart were completely out of the equation, the idea of eating those richer foods still causes me intense anxiety. Just imagining it brings back that tight feeling in my chest and the fear of my belly looking soft or popping out in the mirror. That fear of gaining weight and losing control over my shape is still very real and hard to shake.
If you were told that eating richer foods would not affect your heart or health at all, would you still avoid them mainly because you fear gaining weight or becoming fat?

Yes, even if heart health weren't a factor, the idea of eating richer foods still causes me deep anxiety. I dread the thought of gaining weight, seeing the scale go up, or having my belly look soft and "pop out." Just thinking about losing control of my weight brings a tight, anxious sensation to my chest because I prefer staying lean.

Have you ever had a period when you were clearly underweight but still felt fat or believed you needed to keep losing weight? This helps me tell whether the main issue is fear of weight gain with distorted body image or a different type of eating concern.

Yes, that is exactly what I am experiencing right now. Even though my clothes are hanging off me and the doctors tell me I'm underweight, when I look in the mirror I don't see myself as "too thin" at all. I still see soft spots on my belly that I feel I need to trim down to protect my heart, and I view keeping this weight off as a matter of healthy self-discipline rather than an illness.
When you look at your body, do you ever feel that you are too thin or need to gain weight, or do you still feel you need to lose more weight even when others say you are underweight?

When I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as "too thin" at all; instead, I notice areas like my belly that still look soft and think I could stand to trim down more to keep my heart healthy. I certainly don't feel any need to gain weight. Staying light feels like a disciplined, sensible choice to avoid the kind of health crises my friends have had.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview is most consistent with anorexia nervosa, restrictive type: the patient is clearly underweight, intentionally restricts intake, strongly fears weight gain, expresses persistent desire to lose more weight, and shows body-image disturbance with denial of being too thin despite objective thinness. The health/heart rationale is present, but the core psychopathology of fear of weight gain and relentless weight-loss behavior is prominent.
